title: Executable Playbook Sandbox for Oncall: typed admin actions & safe runner
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a sandboxed, auditable executor for runbooks-as-tasks that lets oncall engineers run typed admin actions safely from the Console and CLI. Goals: (1) Author runbooks as small, composable YAML/JSON playbooks that reference typed actions (eg: rotate-key, drain-host, scale-pool) with explicit input schemas; (2) Provide a dry-run mode, input validation, and a simulated planner so oncall can preview side effects; (3) Enforce RBAC and gating (2-person approval for high-risk ops) and surface fallbacks; (4) Produce structured audit logs and telemetry to Console (per-run token cost, latency, success/failure, rollback triggers); (5) Integrate with existing admin utilities library and the micro-steplet framework so runbooks can be executed locally in dev or in the sandboxed ops environment.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: ticket created after postmortem from INC-2026-02-27 revealed repeated manual host drains. Proposed building a sandboxed playbook runner to reduce burn and provide reproducibility. Assigned to Ravi.

2026-03-03 - Design sync: agreed on typed actions + schema-first validation; decided to use existing micro-operator steplet format (ENG-271443) as the lowest common denom for action wiring. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Executable+Playbook+Sandbox

2026-03-05 - Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/pull/482 - contains an alpha runner, YAML schema, and a dry-run simulator. Initial tests validate schema enforcement and audit logging format.
2026-03-06 - Security review requested: requested security_review_required=true; SRE and SecOps to review KMS usage for secrets referenced by actions. Notes added to PR.

2026-03-08 - Design feedback from PM (Alex Rivera): add 'rollback-safety' flag and explicit side-effect labels so telemetry can trigger automatic follow-up playbooks. Also avoid embedding credentials; use ephemeral tokens.

2026-03-09 - Blocker identified: RBAC gating requires integration with Private control plane SSO tokens; blocked until SSO token passthrough API is available (dependency ENG-832999). Added dependency and mitigations (manual approval path).

2026-03-10 - Implementation update: sandbox runner v0.2 now supports per-action input schemas, dry-run, and structured audit events forwarded to ops-console ingest endpoint. Manual QA checklist created in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/ops/playbook-sandbox/qa-checklist.xlsx
acceptance_criteria: Playbook YAML accepts typed action calls with schema validation and rejects malformed inputs
Dry-run mode produces a deterministic preview of side effects with a clear human-readable plan
Actions execute only after RBAC check; high-risk actions require 2 approvals or a canary flag
Every run produces structured audit events and a linkable run report visible in Console
CLI can run playbooks in a local dev sandbox identical to production runner behavior
